claims.text: Rapid thermal-shock synthesis limits precursor atomic mobility.
Limited atomic mobility kinetically traps the elements in a homogeneous single-phase solid solution.
A high number of elements dilutes the influence of strong pairwise interactions.
With many atom types and limited mobility, stochastic particle formation can produce a homogeneous alloy even when the elements reduce sequentially.
Slower cooling or a longer high-temperature dwell increases atomic mobility.
The additional mobility from slower cooling or longer dwell favors thermodynamically preferred segregation or secondary-phase formation.
The baseline process reaches approximately 1100–2000 K within milliseconds and cools at approximately 10^5 K/s.
Those baseline rapid-shock conditions produce a metastable, homogeneous single-phase solid solution.
Cooling rate or peak-temperature dwell time will be varied while precursor composition and peak temperature are held constant.
Rapid heating promotes precursor decomposition and initial elemental mixing.
Increasing the number of atom types lowers the probability of local ordering or phase segregation.
Rapid cooling freezes atoms in place before significant diffusion occurs.
Relative to rapid cooling, slower cooling or longer dwell will increase elemental segregation or phase separation and cause secondary phases to emerge.
Slower cooling or longer dwell may also change particle morphology and crystal structure.

The hypothesis applies specifically to nanoparticles containing more than five noble-metal components processed at approximately 1100–2000 K with millisecond heating and approximately 10^5 K/s cooling.
The mechanism may not apply to solution syntheses with inherently high precursor mobility or to two-element systems.
The threshold cooling rates and dwell times for the transition to phase separation, and the role of specific elemental interactions, remain unquantified.

The hypothesis is falsified if slower-cooled or longer-dwell samples show no statistically significant increase in phase separation, segregation, or morphology change relative to the rapid-cooled control.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that only the cooling profile is varied, whereas the intervention and experiment also permit varying the high-temperature dwell time, which is a separate processing variable.
